title: Equality of unit sections on a cartesian etale object
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $h:T\to S$ a morphism, $F$ a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], $Q\to S$ and $A\to T$ etale objects [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\times_ST$ be an isomorphism over $T$ and $p:A\to Q$ its first projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $s,t\in F(Q)$, their images under the inverse-image unit for $h$ agree on $Q\times_ST$ if and only if their arbitrary restrictions along $p$ agree on the identity object of $A$. Here arbitrary restriction means the unit for $p$ followed by $Q\to S$, then restriction along $(p,\mathrm{id}_A)$ to the identity object [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units].

source.place: Tag 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero), paragraph after Definition 03S3; Tag 00XZ (section-localize); Tags 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites) and 03CC (definition-composition-morphisms-sites), composition of inverse images and units.

proof.text: Write v=A.hom and B=Q times_S T. The hypothesis on e and p, together with e being a morphism over T, gives p followed by Q.hom = v followed by h. Transport the arbitrary restriction formula along this equality by substituting the composite morphism; this avoids rewriting dependent site instances.

Let E identify the pullback of Q along v followed by h with the iterated pullback along h and v, let d=(p,id), and put dprime=d followed by E.hom. The two pullback projections show that composition of dprime with the localization counit is e.hom after the identity-object isomorphism. Use pullback.hom_ext, the two pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso inverse projection formulas and the hypothesis on p.

The chosen composition isomorphism c for h and v satisfies the composition unit equation. Its naturality for dprime identifies the arbitrary restriction along p with c, evaluated at the identity object of A.left, applied to the restriction of the successive h- and v-units along dprime. Cancellation of E.hom followed by E.inv is the required functor-map calculation.

Choose the etale inverse-image/restriction isomorphism rho for v. Its unit equation at B and naturality for dprime identify the preceding restriction, after rho, with the h-unit at Q followed by F_h restricted along the identity-object isomorphism and e. All three postcomposition maps (c inverse, rho and restriction along these isomorphisms) are isomorphisms in Type, hence injective. Apply this equality to s and t and cancel these maps to obtain the iff.
